predecessors.name: County of Nassau
predecessors.text: the Duchy of Nassau 1806-1814 as the pages name it: the Rheingau, Höchst, Königstein, Cronberg, Lahnstein, Ehrenbreitstein, Limburg, Weilburg, Montabaur, Idstein and Usingen, Sayn-Altenkirchen and…

successors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
successors.text: the whole duchy, annexed by Prussia in 1866 and from 1868 part of the province of Hesse-Nassau

ledger.x: 1806: the Principality of Wied-Neuwied is dissolved under Napoleon's pressure and assigned to the Duchy of Nassau.
1806: Nassau-Usingen and Nassau-Weilburg merge into the Duchy of Nassau on 30 August 1806.
1815: the Orange-Nassau principalities of Dillenburg, Hadamar and Diez come to the Duchy.
1815: Wied-Neuwied, held by Nassau since 1806, falls to Prussia.
1815: Sayn-Altenkirchen, which Nassau held from 1803 (Reichsdeputationshauptschluss of 25 February 1803), goes to Prussia.
1815: Nassau gives border strips near Siegen and Wetzlar to Prussia in the same exchange: 'Dabei gab Nassau Grenzstreifen nahe Siegen und Wetzlar an Preußen ab'.
1816: Weilburg ceases to be the capital and Wiesbaden becomes the sole capital (Duchy page infobox: 'Weilburg (1806-1816); Wiesbaden (1816-1866)').
1866: the occupation ends in annexation, promulgated on 20 September 1866 ('Am 16.
1866: Prussia annexes the Duchy of Nassau on 20 September 1866.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.outcome: Nassau, a member of the Confederation of the Rhine, changed sides on 23 November 1813 and was guaranteed its 'souveränes Fortbestehen' by Russia, Austria and Prussia; the Congress of Vienna settled its boundary in 1815.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: 'When the Austro-Prussian War broke out on 14 June 1866, the Duchy of Nassau took the side of Austria'; the Peace of Prague was dated 23 August 1866 and Prussia annexed Nassau on 20 September 1866.

certainty.note: The duchy was assembled from many small mediatised holdings in 1803-1806 and consolidated into three districts only on 1 August 1809 (German page); no page gives a boundary.
The 1815 exchange with Prussia (Katzenelnbogen, the strips near Siegen and Wetzlar) is the last boundary change on the pages; the Wetzlar exclave of Prussia remained to the east.
